summary: Iteration 6 — Auto-Link Engine + Login side-effect regression: 22/22 pass (100%) on /app/backend/tests/test_auto_link.py. All 12 review-request areas verified: (A) Login side-effects — fresh non-demo user snapshot with 7 seeded decisions is byte-stable across 5 subsequent logins (starts_at, deadline, history event counts all unchanged), confirming _refresh_time_anchors + _ensure_live_imminent do NOT run for normal users; demo user login still yields top decision 'Esci tra 25 minuti.' with 'imminent' in reason_tags; POST /api/admin/demo/refresh → 403 for normal user, 200 {ok:true,email:'demo@ora.app'} for demo. (B) Basic auto-link: bill decision with provider=Enel produces ≥1 proposed proposal on subscription node with confidence≥0.70, ambiguous=false, matcher_version='auto_link/v1.0', matching_signals include both VERIFIABLE_PROVIDER and CATEGORY_TYPE, reason is a non-empty Italian sentence ending with '.', and NO auto-accept (provider is not in VERIFIABLE_TAGS). Decision.node_ids still empty. (C) Auto-accept: decision with metadata.plate=AB123CD auto-accepts via VERIFIABLE_PLATE with confidence=1.0, status='accepted', accepted_by_system=true, accepted_by_user=false; decision.node_ids now contains the car id and life_graph.linked event is recorded (on the DECISION history — see minor issue below). (D) Ambiguity: adding a 2nd subscription node with same provider=Enel then analyzing a Decision{provider:Enel} yields auto_accepted=[] and both proposals flagged ambiguous=true with confidence≥0.60; decision.node_ids untouched. (E) Keyword-only: exam decision on a user with no university node produces zero verifiable signals and no auto-accept, even under /reanalyze force. (F) Idempotence & versioning: back-to-back analyzes on the same steady-state decision return identical proposal ids and identical created_at (no duplicates on (decision,node) pairs among active proposals). Persisted proposal docs contain matcher_version, decision_signature, node_knowledge_version fields; after PATCH bumping subscription provider, active proposals bind to the CURRENT knowledge version. (G) Accept+reject: accept sets status='accepted', accepted_at/accepted_by_user/acceptance_reason, links node_id once even when accept called twice (idempotent); reject sets status='rejected'+rejected_at+correction_reason; re-analyze with unchanged signature does NOT regenerate rejected proposals (suppression works); reanalyze (force) may regenerate while the old rejected doc remains for audit; idempotent reject returns same doc; accept on rejected → 404. (H) Sensitive redaction: neither KNOWLEDGE_PLATE nor VERIFIABLE_PLATE signal descriptions contain 'AB123CD'; response bodies do not embed full knowledge docs. (I) Cross-user isolation: user B gets 404 on analyze/reanalyze/list/get/accept/reject for user A's decision and proposal; unauthenticated requests to every /api/auto-link/* endpoint return 401/403. (J) LifeGraphService integration: two proposals on different nodes for different decisions both auto-accept via VERIFIABLE_CONTRACT and each decision.node_ids gets its target node exactly once. (K) Regression: /decisions/top (limit=3), legacy /priorities, /life-graph/nodes/{id}/graph (depth=2 with root/nodes/edges/distances/decisions), /auth/me 401 all still work. (L) Side effects: 5 analyzes across generic decisions leave the original seeded-decision anchors, life-graph edges count, and knowledge doc count all UNCHANGED. Run command: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_auto_link.py -v -n 0 (serial required — module-scope shared STATE dict).

critical_code_review_comments: Auto-Link module is cleanly isolated (deterministic, no external calls). matcher.py uses pure functions with (decision, node, knowledge, dtext) signature — trivially testable and swappable. Confidence combiner uses saturating product 1-Π(1-c) — transparent, no opaque score.

can_auto_accept(candidate) correctly enforces the triple-gate: confidence≥0.95 AND ≥1 verifiable signal AND not ambiguous. VERIFIABLE_TAGS set matches the spec exactly. VERIFIABLE_PROVIDER intentionally NOT in VERIFIABLE_TAGS (verifiable=False) — correct, provider is not globally unique. Verified empirically: bill+provider produces no auto-accept even at high confidence.

_decision_signature covers title/description/category/metadata/node_ids/linked_to. Any of these mutating invalidates the signature and enables re-generation. Rejection suppression checks decision_signature match — good.

AutoLinkService._apply_accept is idempotent (already-accepted returns current doc), atomic (single link_decision call then a single update_proposal), and self-heals if the underlying node or decision has disappeared (marks EXPIRED with reason). LifeGraphService.link_decision uses $addToSet so duplicate node_ids are impossible — verified in test_12 (2× accept, node_ids has target once).

Sensitive redaction is implemented at the SIGNAL-CONSTRUCTION site (matcher._redact_display), not at the response boundary — safer, because even future consumers of MatchSignal.description cannot leak values. Empirically verified: VERIFIABLE_PLATE description is 'Targa corrispondente' (no value), KNOWLEDGE_PLATE is 'Targa citata nella Decision' (no value).

Cross-user guard: /auto-link/decisions/{id}/proposals endpoint first calls db.decisions.find_one({id, user_id}) before listing — correct order, no proposal existence leak. Every other endpoint in AutoLinkRepository filters by user_id.

Only ONE minor spec drift found: life_graph.linked event lands on the DECISION history, not the NODE history (review §10 wording said 'car's history'). Test accepts either; behavior otherwise correct and idempotent.
